The snow fell softly, blanketing the land in a fresh layer of white. As I stepped into the cozy winter cabin, the scent of wood smoke and pine filled my nostrils. The interior was a stark contrast to the frigid world outside, with its warm colors and inviting light. I unpacked my bags, placing my jacket and boots in the designated spots by the door. The cabin was equipped with a wood-burning stove, and I gathered kindling to start a fire. The crackle of the flames provided a comforting rhythm as I settled into a plush armchair.

Outside, the world was hushed and peaceful. I ventured out to collect more wood from the shed below. The cold bit at my cheeks, but the breath of fresh air felt exhilarating. As I returned to the cabin, I noticed a small bird perched on a branch above. It chirped softly, as if acknowledging my presence. Inside, I added more logs to the fire and wrapped myself in a blanket.

The weekend felt like a retreat from the world, a time to disconnect and reconnect with nature. I spent hours reading by the fire, sipping on hot cocoa, and enjoying the solitude. The cabin felt like a sanctuary, a place of respite and reflection. As night fell, I wrapped up in a quilt and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of the snowy landscape outside.

Making mistakes was part of the process, made each successful float or dive a small victory. Making decisions to push past fears made swimming not just a skill but a newfound freedom.

# Learning to Swim as an Adult

Swimming can be mastered by anyone regardless of age. I started learning to swim in my early thirties because I wanted to enjoy summer activities without sweating and breathlessness. At first classes were challenging breath control and kicking movements were hard to coordinate but with time practice became easier. Instructors were patient and encouraging guiding me through each level. I learned breath control by blowing bubbles in water then moving to kicking on stomach followed by kicking on back. Floating breath control and then swimming strokes came next. Now I can swim several lengths of the pool with ease. More soon.
